questions.q:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

The seat which you are sitting on is my.
questions.s:
The correct answer is 'is my'. 

Key Points

  • The erroneous Part 'is my' should be 'is mine'. 
  • We know that 'mine' is the possessive pronoun of 'I'. And 'mine' can be used as an 'object'. 
    • Example: Save your money as well as mine too. 
  • Whereas, 'my' is the possessive adjective and it is used with object. 
    • Example: This is my book. 
  • Therefore, by reading the above explanation we find that the correct answer is Option 1. 
    ​

The correct sentence is: The seat which you are sitting on is mine.

Additional Information

  • We should avoid 'Possessive Pronouns' with words such as: 
    • Separation, Leave, Excuse, Mention, Report, Pardon, Sight, Favor. ​

Recycling is a key component of modern waste reduction and is the third component of the ‘Reduce, Reuse and Recycle’ waste hierarchy _______ aim is to extract the maximum practical benefits from products and to generate the minimum amount of waste.
questions.s:
The correct answer is 'whose'.

Key Points

  • The most appropriate word for the given blank is 'whose'.
  • The word "whose" is a pronoun used to show possession.
  • In this sentence, the "waste hierarchy" possesses the aim of extracting maximum practical benefits from products and generating the minimum amount of waste.
  • The other options are not appropriate because "who's" is a contraction of "who is" or "who has," "which" is used to refer to things or animals, and "whom" is used as the object of a verb or preposition.
  • Therefore, "whose" is the most appropriate word to use here. 
     

Correct Sentence: Recycling is a key component of modern waste reduction and is the third component of the ‘Reduce, Reuse and Recycle’ waste hierarchy whose aim is to extract the maximum practical benefits from products and to generate the minimum amount of waste.

questions.q:
In the following question, one part of the sentence may have an error. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option.

My opponent is (A)/ a good player and (B)/ very unpredictable, but I am (C)/ mentally tougher than she. (D)
questions.s:
Part D has an error.

A pronoun directly after 'than' or 'as' is usually in the accusative case (objective case) unless there is a verb after it. If a verb follows it, the nominative form (subjective case) is used. Since there is no verb after 'she' (subjective pronoun), it is grammatically incorrect. It should be replaced with the accusative case 'her' (objective pronoun) to rectify the given sentence.

Hence, option (a) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: My opponent is a good player and very unpredictable, but I am mentally tougher than her.
